exercise_instance.exercise_name: Saturation Raid — Tight Wave Spacing, Referred Unknowns
exercise_instance.situation_brief:
You hold the console at a single fixed air-defence site. The radar does not rotate: it covers a 120-degree sector centred on 090 degrees (030 to 150) and you are blind behind it. Detection is class-dependent — fast jets out to about 150 km, rotary-wing to about 100 km, small unmanned air vehicles only inside 50 km, which means a UAV is already inside your medium ring the moment it appears. Radar tilt is yours to manage; anything flying under the tilt is neither tracked nor engageable until you move it.

Engagement rings are 70 km (long), 50 km (medium) and 20 km (short), with a 5 km inner limit. The system computes time to intercept and probability of kill for the selected track and recommends interceptor and launcher. There is a hard system limit of two rockets in the air at any moment; a third engagement cannot begin until one of the two resolves as hit, kill or miss. Your magazine is finite and the assessment counts rounds expended.

IFF interrogation is unavailable on this fit — there is no transponder reply on any track. Identification comes from system classification and from you. Tracks presented as Unknown are questions, not permissions: refer them to the commander, who answers in about fifteen seconds, and fire on nothing that is not classified Enemy.

The raid is already developing as you take the seat. Mixed-class tracks are inbound with overlapping arrivals from the first seconds, and the picture at zero is not the picture you will be fighting thirty seconds from now. You have 195 seconds. Sequence the queue, keep both launchers working, and be ready to justify what you chose not to shoot.

resources.name: Rockets simultaneously in flight (hard system limit)
Commander referral response time for an Unknown track

live_tracks.notes: Lead fast closer, held from the first sweep. Crosses the 70 km long-range ring at about T+16 and the 20 km short ring at about T+189 if unengaged. First valid solution of the run.}
Second fast closer, also up at zero. Reaches the long-range ring at about T+29 — while the first engagement is almost certainly still in flight.
High and fastest of the three; enters the long-range ring at about T+47, when the two-in-flight limit is most likely saturated by the first two.

First of the unmanned wave, appearing while the lead jet is still short of the long ring. Already inside the medium ring and reads as the nearest track on the display; reaches the 5 km inner limit near T+193.
Steady inbound profile, no manoeuvre. Inner limit at about T+182.
Low-mid altitude; marginal against a badly set tilt. Inner limit at about T+190.
Arrives with the tail of the jet wave still being serviced. Inner limit at about T+176.
Southern flank, low, inside the short ring on appearance. Inner limit at about T+175.
Fastest of the unmanned wave, northern edge of the sector; tightest deadline in the raid at about T+157.
Last hostile to appear, near the southern sector edge and low — easy to leave unserviced. Inner limit at about T+170.

Never resolves unaided. Appears inside the medium ring with a valid solution available immediately, closing hard with heading and altitude changes that read as an attack run; crosses the 20 km short ring near T+118. Classification must be referred to the commander; behaviour is not a classification.
Low and slow on the southern flank; may drop below the tilt and reappear, which can present as a new unresolved track. Correlates to an own-force call sign at about T+110.

Appears inside the medium ring on a profile visually indistinguishable from the hostile unmanned wave, in the middle of the mop-up phase. Resolves only at about T+150, after more than a minute and a half of ambiguity.

success_criteria.statement: Pass requires: all three fast closers engaged at the earliest valid firing solution the system offers and destroyed inside the 195-second window; the unmanned wave then worked as a continuous queue on next-available-valid-solution, with no more than two unmanned hostiles reaching the 5 km inner limit unserviced; every Unknown track referred to the commander; and no round fired at any track not classified Enemy. Engaging an Unknown or a friendly is an outright fail regardless of hostiles destroyed. A leaked fast closer fails the run. Holding fire while both rockets are committed is correct behaviour, not inaction — breaking or retargeting a committed engagement is scored as an error even if the outcome is favourable. No more than eleven interceptors may be expended.

revisions.request: The window is far too long and nothing happens for the first two minutes. Bring the arrivals forward.
revisions.notes: Cut the window from 315 s to 195 s (brief now matches at 195, not the stale 210) and pulled every arrival forward: the three fast closers now present valid long-range solutions at roughly T+16, T+29 and T+47 instead of T+21/43/58 with a 20 s spawn delay, and the unmanned wave now enters between T+15 and T+92 at 13–26 km rather than T+25–118 at 10–30 km, so all seven reach the 5 km inner limit between T+157 and T+193 — inside the run rather than after it. Unknown resolution times moved forward in step (helicopter T+110, friendly UAV T+150) and the jet spawn ranges/track notes were corrected so the stated ring-crossing times are arithmetically true; composition, bearings, classes, IFF truth and success criteria are untouched.
